title: Giving AI a seat at the peer review table - Nature Biotechnology
text:
External peer review constitutes a foundational component of science and has been central to the evolution of merit-based research since the eighteenth century. However, time, which is the most essential element that scientists need to complete a thorough and fair review, has become scarce. A manuscript or grant application reviewer must evaluate large amounts of complex data while simultaneously dealing with their own research and grants, clinical duties, teaching, mentoring and administrative responsibilities. As reviewers’ workloads have increased, the basic structure of the peer review process has remained largely unchanged: three scientists evaluate a manuscript or a grant application, while editorial boards and funding agencies make decisions based mainly on the experts’ assessments.Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a multipurpose tool for researchers, and it can perform many tasks of peer reviewers. There is an opportunity here to refocus and strengthen the process of peer review, with AI as a bounded, non-voting, secure, auditable tool — not replacing scientists, but serving as an additional ‘Reviewer 4’.
